info.name: PMIS User Service (port 8001)
info.description:
Postman collection for PMIS-user-management — the authentication + RBAC microservice running on port 8001.

**Endpoints covered** (user-mgmt slice only):
- `POST /api/v3/users/login` (single-stage + 2FA branch)
- `POST /api/v3/users/login/send-otp`, `/login/verify-otp`
- `POST /api/v3/users/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`
- `POST /api/v3/users/refresh`, `/introspect`, `/logout`
- User CRUD: `/users/create`, `/users/{id}`, etc.
- RBAC user-side: `/users/{id}/roles/{role_id}`, `/users/{id}/permissions/{code}`
- Legacy /api/v3/roles, /api/v3/permissions (deprecated; use master/*)
- `/api/v3/master/roles`, `/api/v3/master/permissions`
- `/health`

**`/api/v3/master/notification_templates/*` is no longer here.** Per, that slice moved to notification-service (port 8002) — see `PMIS_Notification_Service.postman_collection.json` in the notification-service repo.

**Project-management endpoints (projects, M/A/T/S, vendors, divisions, etc.) are NOT in this collection.** Call them at the monolith on port 8000 — see `PMIS_API_Collection.postman_collection.json` in the monolith repo.

**Two ways to use this collection:**
1. **Direct (port 8001)** — set `baseUrl` to `http://10.1.131.199:8001`. Hits user-mgmt directly.
2. **Through monolith proxy** — set `baseUrl` to `http://10.1.131.199:8000` AND ensure the monolith has `USER_SERVICE_PROXY_ENABLED=true`. Same URLs work — the monolith's `UserServiceProxyMiddleware` forwards them to user-mgmt transparently.

Both paths give the same result; option 1 is one fewer hop and useful for direct user-mgmt debugging.

request.description: Assign a role to a user

Authenticate user and receive a JWT token. change 3: when 2FA is required for the user (per-user flag + global ``REQUIRE_2FA``), this endpoint returns ``{requires_otp: true, ephemeral_token, channels_available}`` instead of an access_token. The client then calls ``/login/send-otp`` and ``/login/verify-otp``.
Verify the reset token (URL token from email or 6-digit OTP from SMS) and set the new password. Tokens are single-use and expire after ``PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS`` (default 1h).

item.name: Grant a direct permission to a user

request.description: Grant a direct permission to a user

Public token introspection. Returns metadata (active, exp, iat, jti, sub, userId, role, isAdmin) for the supplied access_token and/or refresh_token. NEVER rotates — use POST /users/refresh to mint a fresh access + refresh pair from a valid refresh token. When both tokens are supplied, the response shape becomes {access: {...}, refresh: {...}}.
List a user's roles

query.description: Admin only. When true, soft-deleted users are also returned. Default false hides them.

request.description: List all users with pagination

Hard logout. Revokes the access token (adds its jti to the blacklist) AND clears the user's refresh-token jti. After this call, the just-used access token will be rejected by the auth middleware on every subsequent request, and the refresh token can no longer mint new access tokens. Idempotent.

item.name: Refresh access token (rotates the refresh token too)

request.description: Validates the supplied refresh token and issues a fresh access + refresh pair. The user row's stored refresh_token_jti is rotated atomically — concurrent refreshes with the same token can only succeed once. Response includes accessTokenExpiresAt + refreshTokenExpiresAt so the client can schedule the next preemptive refresh.

item.name: Request a password-reset link or code

request.description: Self-service password reset. Body: ``{login_or_email, channel}``. ``email`` channel sends a clickable reset link; ``sms`` sends a numeric code. ALWAYS returns 200 with a generic message regardless of whether the account exists (anti-enumeration).

Clears deletedAt/deletedBy and sets status='active' on a soft-deleted user. Idempotent on already-active users — returns the current snapshot rather than 409. All project mappings, vendor association, and division values are preserved on disk during soft-delete and re-surface automatically. Mirrors POST /api/v3/vendors/{id}/restore. Path param accepts integer ``id`` or ``US-...`` code.

item.name: Revoke a direct permission from a user

request.description: Revoke a direct permission from a user

Generate + dispatch a 6-digit OTP for an in-progress 2FA login session. Pass the ``ephemeral_token`` returned from ``/login`` plus a chosen channel (``email`` or ``sms``). Resends are rate-limited per ``OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`` (default 60s).

Verify the OTP sent via ``/login/send-otp`` and mint the real access + refresh JWT pair. Same response shape as a non-2FA ``/login`` success. Wrong codes increment a counter; after ``OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS`` (default 5) the OTP row is invalidated and the user must request a new one.

Health check endpoint.

Reports the status of subsystems the app depends on. Currently:
 - the API process itself ("status")
 - file-storage backend reachability (NFS mount in prod, local
 folder in dev) — surfaced separately so ops can distinguish a
 fully-healthy app from one that's serving but can't accept
 attachment uploads.
 - notification client config + reachability — diagnostic for the
 2FA / forgot-password flow. Exposes which backend is selected
 (``mock`` or ``http``), the configured service URL, and a quick
 reachability probe so ops can tell at a glance whether the BE
 will actually dispatch OTP emails or silently sink them in
 the audit table.

The NFS server / export are reported back from settings (informational
— the app doesn't connect to them directly; the OS mount does). They
let ops verify which file store this instance is wired to.

item.name: Role Assignments
List a user's role assignments ( — global / org / project)

request.description: GET /api/v3/users/{id}/role-assignments — Returns every scoped role-assignment row for the user (global, org-scoped, project-scoped) in one list. Replaces the legacy GET /api/v3/users/{id}/roles which only surfaced global user_roles entries. Auth: USERS_READ on self, USERS_READ_ALL on others.

item.name: Grant a scoped role to a user

request.description: POST /api/v3/users/{id}/role-assignments — Body: roleId (int) + exactly one of organizationId / projectId (or both omitted for global). Caller-vs-target gate enforced server-side: super_admin grants any; admin grants any except super_admin; org_admin grants project-tier roles within its vendor; project_admin grants project_member only on its project. Auth: rbac:assign + the caller-vs-target rule.

DELETE /api/v3/users/{id}/role-assignments/{aid} — Revokes a single (user, role, scope) row. Last-super_admin lockout: the only global super_admin row cannot be revoked. Auth: rbac:assign + caller-vs-target.

GET /api/v3/users/{id}/projects — Every project the user is assigned to + the role names they hold on each. Powers the User Mgmt menu landing view. Auth: USERS_READ on self / USERS_READ_ALL on others.

GET /api/v3/projects/{id}/role-assignments — Returns the per-project drill-down: every assignment on the project grouped by role bucket. Powers the FE Project-Mapping mock. NOT proxied through monolith :8000 — set baseUrl to user-mgmt :8001 to call this. Auth: project_members:read.

POST /api/v3/projects/{id}/role-assignments — Body must include userId; project_id comes from the path. Always creates a project-scoped row. NOT proxied through monolith :8000. Auth: rbac:assign + caller-vs-target.

item.name: Revoke a project-scoped role assignment — :8001 only

request.description: DELETE /api/v3/projects/{id}/role-assignments/{aid}. NOT proxied through monolith :8000. Auth: rbac:assign + caller-vs-target.

item.name: Vendor's project map (Org Mgmt landing) — :8001 only

request.description: GET /api/v3/vendors/{id}/projects?expand=role-assignments — Every project owned by the vendor with optional inlined per-role assignment buckets. NOT proxied through monolith :8000 (monolith has its own /vendors/{id}/projects with a different shape). Auth: PROJECTS_READ_ALL OR org_admin of the vendor.

item.description:
— scoped role assignments + project-mapping views.

Three scopes per row in `user_role_assignments`: global (both scope cols NULL), org (`organization_id` set), project (`project_id` set). Caller-vs-target gate enforced by `app/api/v3/role_assignments/services.can_caller_grant`.

All eight endpoints here are user-mgmt-owned and reachable directly on port 8001. Set baseUrl to `http://127.0.0.1:8001` (or the deploy host's :8001) when running this collection.

See `C:/Programming/PMIS/DOC_41_FLOWS.md` for the full flow narrative.
